subject: Request: Quantico Health POC - temporary SLO deviation & pricing concession
messages:
From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@quantico.health>

Cc: procurement@quantico.health
Date: Mon, 2 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quantico: POC SLO & terms for evaluation

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's latency profile and the console visibility. We're moving forward with a time-boxed POC (6 weeks) to validate integration with our patient-intake workflows, but we have two asks before we can sign the POC SOW:

1) Temporary SLO deviation: Our infra will route synthetic traffic that inflates tail latency by design. For the POC period we need a documented temporary latency SLO of 200ms p50 / 900ms p95 and a relaxed uptime target of 97% (instead of your standard 99.9%). We understand this is non-standard — please confirm if Redwood can issue a formal SLO variance for 60–90 days and what remedies/service credit cap would apply.

2) Commercial concession: As this is a reference POC with potential enterprise rollout across 3 regions, we'd like an early-bird 12% discount on committed monthly capacity for the first 6 months, contingent on meeting basic adoption metrics.

I've attached a short SOW and the Quantico procurement playbook for reference. We need internal approvals on our side by Friday to hit our integration window. Can you route this to your deal desk and let us know the approval path and expected turnaround?

Appreciate it — Alex

--

Rishi / Aditya — reviewed. Position and constraints below.

1) Temporary SLO variance: We can grant a limited 90-day SLO variance to 97% uptime for the POC, with the following controls:
   - Remedy: service credit up to 15% of monthly POC fees (not an unlimited percentage).
   - Cap: maximum single-month credit capped at $25k for the POC period.
   - Monitoring: Quantico agrees to baseline traffic profile and provide a narrow window for synthetic test runs; any traffic that violates the agreed test window will void the variance.

2) Commercial concession: 12% early-bird discount is acceptable for first 6 months only if:
   - Quantico signs a 6-month committed capacity agreement for the POC and provides a signed adoption KPI appendix (Adoption KPI: >= 5k inference calls/day by end of month 3).
   - Finance (Lauren) to confirm revenue recognition and margin impact. If Lauren signs off, this can be approved without exec escalation.

Please note legal will require a short amendment to the MSA to capture the variance and remedy caps. Marissa recommending we include a hard expiration date on the variance (90 days from start of POC) and an automatic roll-to-standard SLO after the POC unless renegotiated.

Lauren — please confirm whether the discount is within delegated authority or if we need finance director signoff.

If finance needs extra runway, I'll escalate to VP level, but hoping to keep this within deal-desk to meet Quantico's timeline.

-Marissa

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and materials. Quick update from our side after internal review:

1) SLO variance: We can approve a 90-day variance to 97% uptime for the POC period with the following remedies and controls:
   - Service credit: up to 15% of the monthly POC fee for qualifying months, with a hard cap of $25,000 per month.
   - Terms: variance applies only when traffic falls within the agreed synthetic test windows; any deliberate traffic patterns outside that will void the variance.
   - Documentation: we'll provide an amendment to the MSA capturing the variance and the explicit expiration date (90 days from POC start).

2) Commercial concession: We can offer a 12% early-bird discount on committed monthly capacity for the first 6 months of the POC, conditional on:
   - A signed 6-month committed capacity SOW and an adoption KPI appendix (>= 5k calls/day by EoM month 3).
   - Execution of the MSA amendment and the SOW prior to POC start.

Next steps: Aditya will post the adoption KPI appendix and the updated term-sheet (redwood-pricing-term-sheet-v3.xlsx) with tracked redlines. Once Quantico confirms the KPI appendix and signs the SOW, Legal will produce the MSA amendment and we will circulate a DocuSign link for signature.

Target: get final signed SOW + amendment by Friday 5/6 to maintain integration schedule. Let us know if you need the remedy language tightened or if procurement needs additional evidence (SOC2 logs, uptime history).

Best,
Rishi
